# Local I/O — 1-Wire, GPIO, sysfs

Format is defined in [`README.md`](README.md). Written 2026-07-31 from the
`equipment-catalog-sweep` journal.

**How complete this is.** The sweep was stopped during verification, so
refutation is partial. Every dialect below says whether a refuter actually
checked it. Anything unchecked is marked `unverified` and must not be built
on — that is the same thing the workflow would have done, not a shortcut.

**Tiers and prices are absent.** Retail sightings were deduped per *model*
during discovery, but the research phase returns model names as plain
strings, so a model here cannot be joined back to the shop that sold it. A
Tier column would have to be guessed, and a guessed tier is worse than none.

## Generator remote-start inputs — the class, not a support list

Swept 2026-09-01 (three parallel research passes: Honda and its 2-wire kits,
the standby/ATS "2-wire start" class with two universal genset controllers,
and the portable market). The entries below are here for one reason: the
generator board closes a maintained dry contact, and its relays, fuse and
surge parts must be chosen for **every input of this class**, not for the one
generator this site owns. `README.md` says why a generator start contact has
no picker list — two wires and a relay have no protocol to be right about, and
a list would imply the makes absent from it do not work. Nothing here changes
that; these entries document the *interface*, its published electrical
envelope, and which popular models have no wired input at all, so nobody
researches them twice.

What the sweep settles, and what it cannot:

- **Four shapes exist.** *2-wire maintained dry contact* (closed = run,
  open = stop; the class this design targets — GenStart on Honda, every
  standby brand's ATS input, DSE, ComAp). *3-wire momentary START + STOP*
  (Onan RV QG, Yamaha's remote connector, Honda's own EU7000is remote block,
  Magnum's EU3000is harness) — a different behaviour, not supported by the
  maintained-contact design. *Switched DC input* (Cummins QuietConnect,
  Samlex EXT.SW above). *Wireless fob only* (Champion, Westinghouse iGen,
  Firman, DuroMax) — no wired input exists.
- **Almost nobody publishes the figures that size a relay.** Open-circuit
  voltage and wetting current on the generator's own input are `?` on every
  generator manual read. The universal controllers do publish theirs — DSE
  12 V / 6 mA typical, ComAp 4.2 kΩ (~3 mA at 12 V) — and Cummins states a
  14 V design voltage. Every 2-wire input read is *switched to battery
  negative*, a few milliamps behind a pull-up. That is the dry-circuit range
  where plain silver contacts fail to make; the relay wants gold-clad or
  bifurcated contacts, and the fuse and TVS want a 30 V class. A meter on the
  site's own input remains the only way to write a number for it
  (`CONTROLLER-V1.md`, "Still to confirm with GenStart").
- **Opening the contact is not always a stop.** Generac runs about a minute
  of cool-down, Kohler five minutes by default, DSE its return-delay and
  cooling timers; Onan stops immediately; GenStart states no timer at all.
  Proof of running at the panel must therefore tolerate an *expected* period
  of AC after a stop command, or every normal stop raises a concern.
- **On the portable market the Honda + 2-wire kit path is nearly alone.**
  The best-selling portables are fob-only, the Westinghouse "ST Switch" is a
  proprietary 7-pin connector that also carries battery charge, and Honda's
  and Yamaha's own remote connectors are 3-wire. The choice of an EU3000is
  with a GenStart kit was the right one and this is the evidence.

### What the other end of the wire publishes

Generator makers stay silent about their inputs; the products that *start*
generators publish the contact they use, and a handful of people have put a
meter on an input. Swept 2026-09-01 (checked that day).

| Start-side product | Contact | Isolated | Note on 2-wire start |
|---|---|---|---|
| Victron Cerbo GX relay 1 | 6 A @ ≤30 VDC · 1 A @ ≤70 VDC · 6 A @ 125 VAC · changeover | yes | Wire the generator's 2-wire input straight to COM/NO; timing relays only for pulse-start Onans; "do not wire this directly to the starter motor or fuel solenoid" |
| Magnum ME-AGS-N RY1–RY3 | ≤5 A, form A | yes | A ≤5 A fuse is **mandatory** on every relay even on a dry-contact circuit; external relay only above ~5 A; Generac PowerPact: relay 1 direct to 178/183 |
| OutBack FX AUX | 12 VDC *output*, ≤800 mA | no | Interposing relay required — the generator "expects dry contact" |
| OutBack Radian AUX · MATE3 relay | 10 A @ 30 VDC · 5 A @ 30 VDC | yes | "provides no voltage of its own" |
| Schneider Conext AGS | 12 V nominal, 30 VDC max, 5 A, NO | yes | "Two-wire start generators are highly recommended" |
| MidNite Classic AUX 1 | 12 V / 200 mA, dry-contact mode PTC-fused | optional | "Recommended that you have a relay in line … isolating the Classic from possible stray voltage sources" |
| Sol-Ark 15K pins 7–8 | 12 V, 100 mA, NO | yes | "must have a two-wire start (dry-contact, normally open)" |
| Deye · Sunsynk G-start | not rated · "approximately 1 A 12 V" | yes | dry contact |
| EG4 6000XP GEN · Growatt SPF | 5 A @ 250 VAC · 3 A @ 250 VAC | yes | — |
| SMA Sunny Island relay 1 | 1 A @ 250 VAC; DC by derating curve only | yes | default = generator request |

|---|---|---|---|---|

| Onan 4000 MicroQuiet (3-wire) | start = red to ground; green 12 V off; blue 12 V running | ? | mygrandrv https://www.mygrandrv.com/threads/remote-generator-start-with-victron-cerbo-gx-mod-success.73839/ | `community-single` |
| Generac 50 kW 3-phase 178/183 | 2.8–31.4 VAC oscillating with the ATS connected, 0.43 VAC without | ? | gentekpower forum https://gentekpower.com/forums/viewtopic.php?t=7435 — an anomaly on an in-phase monitor, not a spec | `unverified` |
| GenStart on Honda, Kohler 3/4, Champion fleX TB2, Briggs 4/5 | ? | ? | the manuals say "close the contact" and nothing else | — |
| GenMon (jgyates/genmon) | no 2-wire electrical data; the maintainer's advice is to use the controller's built-in two-wire mode | — | https://github.com/jgyates/genmon/issues/835 | `community-single` |

What it settles for the generator board:

- **The industry's output is an isolated normally-open contact in the 5 A /
  30 VDC class** (Magnum, Conext, MATE3, Cerbo, EG4), with three signal-level
  outliers (Sol-Ark 100 mA, MidNite 200 mA, Sunsynk ~1 A). Ours is the same
  class, plus what none of them state: contacts that still make at the
  milliamps a Generac or DSE input actually draws.
- **Nobody documents the dry-circuit problem.** The only wetting current
  published anywhere is DSE's 6 mA, and Generac's 5 V current-limited input
  lives in a diagnostic manual. Gold-clad or bifurcated contacts are the
  answer the field has not written down.
- **Not every "2-wire" input is a logic input.** DynaGen's carries crank
  current — 20 A peak — through the contact. A set like that gets an
  interposing relay at the generator, as OutBack already requires for its
  12 V AUX; the 60 ft pair and the board's contact are never asked to carry
  it. Sizing the fuse at 5 A (Magnum's mandate, GenStart's kit fuse) makes
  that boundary a blown fuse, not a welded contact.
- **Voltage found: 5 VDC (Generac, vendor) to ~12.4 V (community), 12 V
  typical. Current: 6 mA to 20 A peak.** A 30 V TVS covers every reading
  that was a reading.

**Reports with no `MetricKind`, for every entry below:** the start input is
an *output* of the controller, so nothing is reported over it. `generator-
run-state` is not read here — it is inferred from proof of AC at the panel
(the PZEM-016 on RS-485 #3), which is the only honest source. Two things the
contract cannot express and every one of these interfaces has: the
*commanded* state of our own contact as distinct from an observed one, and
the vendor cool-down window during which "stopped" is neither true nor a
fault.
